drills.title: Zone It!
drills.description: Drop each item into the right zone. Speed counts — the scene is building itself around you.

items.why: Command lives in the cold zone, visible and safe.
The hazard source defines the hot zone.
Definitive field treatment happens in the cold zone.

items.prompt: Casualty collection point during an active-shooter response
items.why: CCPs sit in the warm (indirect threat) zone, staffed by Rescue Task Forces with security.
Staging is cold, remote, and out of sight of the hazard.

items.prompt: Direct-threat area where the shooter is still active
items.why: Direct threat = hot zone; law enforcement neutralizes the threat.

items.prompt: Applying a tourniquet under police escort in a cleared hallway
items.why: Indirect-threat care (TECC) happens in the warm zone.
Media are kept in the cold zone, away from patients.
LZ is cold and away from treatment because of rotor wash.

items.prompt: Collapsed floor slabs with trapped victims and ongoing aftershocks
items.why: Unstable structure = hot zone; USAR teams only.
Rehab supports responders in the cold zone.
